doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Joining Basie at thirty and never quitting
summary: He says he joined Basie at 30, dyed his hair for press as the young blonde drummer, and never considered quitting.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: It’s just like life. But you really have to I think if you want it bad enough, you’ve got to stick with it very very deeply. I stuck with it long enough. See I didn’t join the Basie band until I was 30. And I’m 50 now and it was incredible. Everybody says, “wow you were a young kid when you were with Basie.” I say, “No, I wasn’t a young kid, I just, I had a young face, and I weight about ten pounds less than I do now and I dyed my hair.” Because we had one of those things, my hair bleached out about the second or third month I was on the band and I started getting some press, a newspaper thing about the young, blonde, white drummer with the Basie band. I said, “AHA — young BLONDE white drummer,” I can use this. So, you know for years Loreal and Clairol were good friends of mine. And it worked, I was the young, blonde, white drummer, instead of the young, white drummer. So that worked along too. But I stuck with it for, well let me say I’ve been playing now professionally, it’s pretty young compared to some of these great giants in there. I’ve got my first musician’s union card 35 years ago. And I started playing on a drum six years before that. So I’ve been playing 41 years, or had something to do with drums for 41 years. And like I said, when I went with the Basie band I was already 30 years old. And sometimes that’s a little late. You know people think well if I haven’t made it by the time I’m 30 I’m just going to give it up. I never thought about quitting. Never ever thought about that. I thought about killing myself. But I never thought about quitting. Well, you know, sometimes you just say — but I never ever once said I’m going to give it up.
